summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was admitted for acute dyspnea and profound fatigue. She presented with symptoms concerning for hyperkalemia, including generalized weakness and exertional dyspnea. Labs confirmed hyperkalemia (K 6.3) and metabolic acidosis, and imaging revealed mild pulmonary edema due to fluid overload. She underwent emergent hemodialysis with successful correction of electrolyte abnormalities and symptomatic improvement. Her subtherapeutic INR (1.4) was addressed with a supplemental warfarin dose, and she was advised to continue her home medications, including those for GERD and dry eyes. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to maintain dialysis, monitor symptoms, and follow up for INR monitoring.
